clue.text: Play presented over and over again

definitions.text: Play presented over and over again

parts.words: Play presented over and over again
parts.note: a sport whose play is divided into overs, bowled one after another, reads like a show given repeatedly

explanation.surface: A stage show that is put on again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is a set of six balls in cricket, the bat-and-ball game; the play comes in over after over.
explanation.definitionFit: The bat-and-ball sport is played in a series of six-ball overs, so its play is literally presented over and over.

clue.text: Painter who may take one in ?

definitions.meaning: John, the English landscape artist who painted The Hay Wain
a police officer who may take someone into custody

explanation.surface: An artist who might give someone lodging or fool them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take one in' looks like deceiving or housing someone; here it is arresting them.
explanation.definitionFit: The English landscape artist shares his name with a police officer, who arrests people.

clue.text: Put in, soldier to turn 27 back

indicators.note: turn says the run of words for put, in and soldier is read in reverse

parts.note: to set something down is to put it
taken as written
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier is posted inside and made to turn back.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 27-across written backwards, which gives a verb meaning sets alight; 'turn' reverses SET, IN and GI.
explanation.definitionFit: Read in reverse, the 27-across entry spells a verb for setting alight, which this word also means.

clue.text: Assistant to cook general

definitions.meaning: a worker employed in a kitchen
Lord ..., the British field marshal of the First World War recruiting poster

explanation.surface: Someone who helps the cook in general.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Kitchener was the British field marshal whose face was on the First World War recruiting poster.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen servant, and the surname of the famous British field marshal.

clue.text: Ends hand-outs

definitions.meaning: the points at the far ends of things
gratuities given to waiters and porters

explanation.surface: Finishes giving out charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Points at the extremities, and gratuities given for service.

clue.text: Plants game shot in here

indicators.note: the word in tells us the game shot is placed inside the word for this place

parts.note: taken as written
a bag is the quantity of game shot by a hunter

explanation.surface: A hunter brings down game among the greenery in this spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbage is grass and other herbaceous vegetation collectively, a general word for plants.

clue.text: Tory angle? Greatest side in opposition

definitions.text: Tory angle? Greatest side in opposition

parts.words: Tory angle? Greatest side in opposition
parts.note: a Tory is on the political right, so a Tory angle is a right angle, and the longest side of a triangle lies opposite it

explanation.surface: Conservative policy, with the biggest party sitting on the opposition benches.
explanation.walkthrough: Political words disguise geometry: the Tories are the right, so the angle is a right angle, and 'opposition' means facing it.
explanation.definitionFit: In a right-angled triangle the longest side is the one opposite the right angle.

clue.text: One may be over six feet, seated

definitions.text: One may be over six feet, seated

parts.words: One may be over six feet, seated
parts.note: a person on horseback sits above six feet in all, the horse's four and the person's own two

explanation.surface: Someone very tall, but sitting down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over six feet' reads as height; it counts the feet of horse and person together.
explanation.definitionFit: A horseman sits astride a horse, so above the horse's four feet and with two of their own.

clue.text: New York street-crossers

parts.note: in Manhattan's grid the north-south thoroughfares run across the numbered east-west streets

explanation.surface: Pedestrians crossing the road in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'street-crossers' suggests pedestrians; in Manhattan the long north-south roads cross the numbered streets.
explanation.definitionFit: Manhattan's north-south thoroughfares carry the name of broad roads and run across its streets.

clue.text: Name of an Irish sea monster, patently

indicators.note: patently means plainly visible, so the letters are openly on view within the words

explanation.surface: Claims to be the name of an Irish sea serpent, obviously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patently' (openly) tells us the name lies in plain view inside 'sea monster'.
explanation.definitionFit: Eamon is a common Irish male first name, the Irish form of Edmund.

clue.text: Music causing delay at court?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Music causing delay at court?' gives no wordplay for NONET; likely an OCR drop (perhaps 'no delay'), unconfirmed without a scan.

clue.text: Fanciful origin of 'PLUTO

parts.note: PLUTO was the wartime pipeline laid under the Channel; its beginning sounds like a mere fantasy, while also literally a dream of a pipe

explanation.surface: Asks where the name of the dwarf planet came from.
explanation.walkthrough: PLUTO (Pipe-Line Under The Ocean) was the Second World War fuel pipeline to France, so its origin was a pipe; the solver thinks of the planet or the cartoon dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe dream is a fanciful hope, and PLUTO began as a dream of a pipe beneath the sea.

clue.text: Peevish and so on, in your old-fashioned setting

indicators.note: in shows the phrase for 'and so on' going inside the old form of your
setting means the archaic pronoun acts as a mount or frame round the other piece

parts.note: thy is the archaic form of your
etc is the abbreviation of et cetera, and so on

explanation.surface: Grumbling 'and so on' in a quaint, old-fashioned way of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetchy and peevish are synonyms, both meaning irritable and quick to take offence.

clue.text: Open with holder of Ashes as protagonist

parts.note: to open something is to start it
the Ashes, the England-Australia cricket trophy, is a small urn

explanation.surface: A batsman opening the innings for the side holding the Ashes trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the cricket series between England and Australia, whose trophy is a tiny urn said to hold burnt bails.
explanation.definitionFit: A star turn is the main act or leading performer, the central figure of a show.

clue.text: Learning the Sisyphean task of heraldic: ornamentation

clue.text: Scholar's not out, so bowl!

parts.note: a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a scholar; with the possessive S
a batsman who is not out is still in

explanation.surface: A cricket captain urging a bowler on because a studious batsman remains unbeaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowl' reads as a cricket order, but it is the noun, a basin.
explanation.definitionFit: A basin is a round open vessel, a kind of bowl.

clue.text: Agreement to study the numbering, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the pieces are spoken and give a word of the same sound

parts.note: con means study and a census is a numbering of the population

explanation.surface: People agree to examine the figures from the population count.
explanation.definitionFit: A consensus is general agreement reached by a group.

clue.text: Goal for an evening out?

parts.note: a goal that evens out the score, read as the aim of a night on the town

explanation.surface: What someone hopes to achieve on a night out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evening out' reads as a night out; it means making the score even.
explanation.definitionFit: A goal that levels the score in a match is the one that makes it even.

clue.text: Smart winter wear, say, for a tree

parts.note: spruce means neat and smart in appearance

indicators.note: say signals that the word for winter wear is spoken and gives a tree's name

parts.note: fur is worn for warmth in winter

explanation.surface: Fashionable cold-weather clothes, for example, chosen in place of a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The spruce fir is a coniferous evergreen, a kind of tree.

clue.text: Bans some barge manoeuvres

indicators.note: manoeuvres suggests the letters of the two words are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Restrictions placed on how certain canal boats may be steered.
explanation.definitionFit: Embargoes are official prohibitions, especially on trade, so they are bans.

clue.text: Music-maker to perch on outside circle

parts.note: the bass is a fish of the perch family

indicators.note: outside means the little word on goes round the ring shape

parts.note: taken as written
a circle is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A musician trying to sit on the outer edge of a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perch' looks like a verb, but it is the fish, a bass.
explanation.definitionFit: The bassoon is a double-reed woodwind instrument, a maker of music.

clue.text: Houseman booked — 'e asks for silence?

definitions.meaning: the master of the house in a book, Roderick of Poe's tale The Fall of the House of
a court official who calls for quiet in the courtroom

explanation.surface: A hospital junior doctor reserved, and he wants everyone to be quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Houseman' suggests a junior hospital doctor, but here it is the man of the house in Poe's story.
explanation.definitionFit: Poe's Roderick heads the House of that name in the book, and a court official of that title calls for silence.

clue.text: Hotly contested this race-for the far crease?

definitions.text: Hotly contested this race-for the far crease?

parts.words: Hotly contested this race-for the far crease?
parts.note: a contest fought fiercely, and a cricket batsman's dash to make the far crease safely

explanation.surface: A fiercely fought sprint to the other end of the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman runs to the crease at the far end of the pitch to score; the crease is a line marking safety.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiercely contested race is one that is strenuously run, as is a batsman's sprint for the far crease.

clue.text: Game to promote a dance assembly

parts.note: to push a product is to promote it
a ball is a formal gathering for dancing

explanation.surface: Organising a dance as a way of advertising something.
explanation.definitionFit: Pushball is a team sport in which a huge ball is pushed towards the opposing goal.

clue.text: Booked juniors on the train

parts.note: leaves of a book, and young attendants holding up a bride's long train

explanation.surface: Children with reserved seats on a railway journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' suggests a railway; it is a wedding dress train, carried by young attendants.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaves in a book share their name with young attendants who carry a bride's train.

clue.text: Strangely long note, B perpetually rising

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word for perpetually is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: ever means always, perpetually

explanation.surface: A note that is oddly sustained, B forever climbing in pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strangely' because the word comes from Latin brevis, short, yet it is the longest note value.
explanation.definitionFit: A breve is a note of eight beats, though its name derives from the Latin for short.

clue.text: Unusually round figure of a churchman

indicators.note: unusually says the letters of the shape's name are arranged in an unusual order

parts.note: a circle is a round figure in geometry

explanation.surface: A clergyman of oddly round shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' rearranges CIRCLE, the round figure, into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleric is a member of the clergy, a churchman.

clue.text: Finish with an organ piece

definitions.meaning: to finish is to come to a halt
a knob on an organ that controls a set of pipes

explanation.surface: Ending with part of a church instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt is to finish, and an organ has knobs controlling ranks of pipes by that name.

clue.text: Plant strong enough to support a bird

definitions.meaning: a weed of the beet family named for its leaf shape

definitions.text: strong enough to support a bird
definitions.meaning: the webbed limb a large waterfowl stands on bears its weight

explanation.surface: A plant sturdy enough for a bird to perch on.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant is named for its webbed leaves, and a waterfowl's foot holds that bird up.

clue.text: Shoots back to finish off a letter

indicators.note: back tells us the word for shoots is read from end to start

parts.note: to shoot a gun is to fire it, so shoots means fires

explanation.surface: Someone fires a shot in return before completing a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A serif is the small stroke finishing off the main strokes of a printed letter.

clue.text: Accommodation on board for a tanner

definitions.text: Accommodation on board for a tanner

parts.words: Accommodation on board for a tanner
parts.note: a sunbather is a tanner, and a ship has an open upper area for them

explanation.surface: Lodging on a ship for a leather worker, or for an old sixpence.
explanation.walkthrough: A tanner is a leather worker, or British slang for an old sixpence coin; here it is someone getting a suntan.
explanation.definitionFit: The open upper level of a ship is where passengers lie out to get a tan.

clue.text: East to West in contractual relationship

definitions.meaning: in bridge, the player sitting East plays with the one sitting West as a pair
a person sharing a business under a contract with another

explanation.surface: Travelling across the globe in a relationship bound by contract.
explanation.walkthrough: In the card game bridge, players are named by compass points and East and West play as a team.
explanation.definitionFit: East and West are a bridge pair, and a business associate shares a firm by contract.
